title: SQL migrations I: extensions, identity/tenancy, RBAC tables, partitioning function, audit_log, reference_sequences
objective: Convert the foundation portion of the Liquibase changelogs to ordered plain-SQL Supabase migrations: required extensions, tenants, users (with auth_user_id), user_tenants, the full RBAC table set, the partition-creation SQL function, audit_log, and reference_sequences — preserving A-12 conventions (bigint PKs, LIST partitioning on tenant_id, composite (tenant_id,id) keys) (M-08).
scope: Migration: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS for pg_cron, pgmq, pg_net (if not already landed in T-002)
tenants (bigint PK, name required, contact fields, status Active/Removed soft-remove, created/updated audit columns)
users (bigint PK, auth_user_id uuid UNIQUE referencing auth.users(id), first/last/email, is_active, last_tenant_id, theme), user_tenants

RBAC: permissions (seed-ready catalog table), roles, role_permissions, user_roles (tenant-context), user_permissions, user_groups, group_members, group_roles, group_permissions — per-tenant/global scoping columns preserved from the changelogs
Partition-creation SQL function (create_tenant_partitions or the ported name) + default partition safety net, faithful to the existing functions/ changelog
audit_log (tenant-scoped where applicable, jsonb before/after payloads), reference_sequences (per-tenant/year sequence rows used by lead ref allocation)
All constraints, uniques (tenant-inclusive), FKs, and indexes for these tables carried over from changelogs 010+
implementation_details: Source of truth: src/api/db/changelog 010-foundation onward + functions/ — convert semantics faithfully, not mechanically; each migration file gets a header comment noting source changelog(s) and rollback/recovery notes for risky steps (M-10).
Naming: supabase/migrations/<timestamp>_<slug>.sql ordered so db reset applies cleanly from empty.

auth.users FK nuance: users.auth_user_id is uuid referencing auth.users(id); app users keep bigint PKs (A-12). Confirm the local stack allows FKs to auth schema; if hosted Supabase discourages a hard FK, use a validated nullable uuid + index and document the decision in the migration header.

Tenant-scoped tables in this batch that are partitioned in the current schema must be created LIST-partitioned on tenant_id with composite (tenant_id,id) primary keys and a DEFAULT partition; the partition function creates per-tenant partitions for all partitioned tables and is invoked later inside the tenant-creation transaction (T-016).
timestamptz UTC everywhere; created_at/updated_at/created_by/updated_by on mutable tables; numeric(18,2) reserved for money columns in later batches.
Validate with supabase db reset after each file; keep files reviewable (one cohesive area per file rather than one giant migration).

integration: supabase db reset applies all migrations from clean state without error (M-10)
SQL assertions: partition function creates partitions for a new tenant id across all partitioned tables in this batch; default partition exists
Constraint checks: duplicate tenant-scoped unique violations rejected; users.auth_user_id uniqueness enforced
Schema-shape comparison against the .NET reference database for this table subset (column names/types/nullability/indexes) — documented diff must be empty or explained

history.message: Task generated by Planner from approved spec.md. Maps to M-08, M-10, A-12, section 11 identity/tenancy + RBAC model.

Delegated to Implementor. T-003 and T-007 run in parallel: disjoint file sets (supabase/migrations vs src/server/lib/config+logging). Harness JSON is owned by the orchestrator during parallel execution to avoid concurrent-write corruption.

Implementor completed T-003. 6 migration files (tenants, users_and_tenancy, rbac, audit_log, reference_sequences, partition_function) applying after T-002's extensions migration. Hard FK auth_user_id -> auth.users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT chosen and documented with a hosted-environment fallback. create_tenant_partitions made CATALOG-DRIVEN instead of the source's hardcoded 22-table array (Liquibase runOnChange has no plain-SQL equivalent, and T-003 cannot name tables T-004/T-005 create) - flagged as a deliberate mechanism change for evaluator review. Orchestrator independently verified: FK fires (users_auth_user_id_fkey error on bad uuid), partitioned tables = user_tenants + reference_sequences, 16 public tables. Open flag: audit_log ported as single `details jsonb` (mapping details->'before'/'after') per the Liquibase/.NET source rather than two columns, though spec 11 wording says 'jsonb before/after payloads' - evaluator must judge against AC-006.

Evaluator PASS at iteration 0. Independently verified: supabase db reset exit 0 (7 migrations from clean); CONVERGENCE proven (implementor had deferred it): reset twice + pg_dump --schema-only diff empty except the per-run pg_dump restrict-token line (not schema content). RULING AC-006 audit_log: single details jsonb carrying before/after keys IS COMPLIANT - AC-006 operative clause is parity with the Liquibase source (which defines one details jsonb); two columns would fail the AC own parity requirement and the parity suite; spec s11 "jsonb before/after payloads" describes payload content, not column count; A-12 jsonb-only-for-audit satisfied. T-013 should add a writer-side test pinning the {before,after} key contract. RULING partition mechanism: catalog-driven create_tenant_partitions APPROVED - membership rule proven exactly equivalent to the source 22-entry array against the live reference DB (22/22, zero drift either direction); probe partitioned table created post-migration was picked up (partition created, insert landed), LIST-on-other-column and RANGE-on-tenant_id decoys correctly excluded; idempotent on re-invocation; DEFAULT partitions present on user_tenants + reference_sequences. Strictly stronger than the source. Parity suite proven non-hollow: evaluator-injected drift column (users.evaluator_drift) turned the suite red naming the exact column; allow-list (5 entries) is honest - each entry existence-asserted on its expected side and the swapped constraint/index shapes are independently asserted in schema-foundation.test.ts. Constraint suite asserts SQLSTATEs (23505/23503/23514) per violation, not catalog existence. Full suite 17 files / 291 tests exit 0; typecheck 0; lint 0. No secrets in migrations. CI wiring of migration validation remains with T-010 (per AC-004 task mapping).
